content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

I'm starting in Phase 1 (Facilitation), Step 1: Goal exploration. Before anything about how it's built, I'd like to understand what you're really after.

You mentioned saving and managing bookmarks. Let me ask about the goal behind it:

- **When this is finished, what should be different from how you handle things today?** In other words, what problem with your current way of keeping links are you hoping to solve?

- Is **saving and managing bookmarks** the heart of it — or is that a means to something bigger (say, finding things again quickly, sharing collections with others, or reading later)?

I ask because the same words can point at quite different apps. Once I understand the "why," I'll play back what I heard to make sure I've got the direction right — and then I'll show you working screens to react to, rather than talking in the abstract.

Right now my links are scattered across browser bookmarks, open tabs, and notes, so I often can’t find something when I need it—or I save it twice.

The heart of the app is having one dependable place where I can save a link quickly, organise it, search for it later, and open the original page. I’d also like to separate things I intend to read from things I’m simply keeping for reference, without losing either.

So the bigger goal is really retrieval: I want confidence that something I saved months ago will be easy to find again. This is mainly for my own use; sharing collections isn’t a priority.

Yes, that’s the right direction, especially the emphasis on being able to find things again.

I picture it primarily as a web app that I can use on both my computer and phone. I’d most often save links while browsing, then return later—usually on my computer—to search, organise, or read them. It doesn’t need to be a separate mobile or desktop app.

**What's settled (12 flows):**
- **Save** a link fast (one box, one click), with a quick review of the page's fetched title/description/preview/icon that you can correct; **duplicates** send you to the existing entry; **save-anyway** when a page's details can't be loaded; a gentle nudge on a non-address.
- **Find** by live, case-insensitive search across title, description, address, tags and notes — with **"quoted phrases"**, **and/or/not**, parentheses, and **#tag**.
- **Organise**: a **To read** reading list you can mark read; **Reference** (everything not to-read); **Archive**/restore; permanent **Delete** with a clear confirmation; freeform **tags** with autocomplete; **Markdown notes**; edit any field including the address.
- **Graceful states**: empty collection, empty views, no results, long text that wraps/clamps.

**One scope question before I propose building** — asked plainly, not technically:

Since you'll use this on both your **computer and phone**, your saved links need to live in **one shared place** both devices reach. Do you want it protected by a **personal sign-in** (so only you can get to your collection), or is it enough to keep it as just your own private copy with **no sign-in** for now?

Your answer decides whether a login is part of what I build. Once you've settled that, I'll ask for your go-ahead to **start implementing this scope**.

- Import and export a standard browser-bookmarks HTML file, retaining titles, tags, and original saved dates where available.

I've verified the edge situations for the six new blocks. Here's the pass — grouped by the kinds of edge we check, with a couple you can see live and the rest confirmed by behaviour:

**Absence of data**
- **Sorting/paging an empty view or empty collection** shows the calm empty state, no broken controls.
- **A saved search that now matches nothing** reopens to the clear "No bookmarks match…" state, with the count reading `0 of N` — try clicking a saved chip whose tag you've since removed.
- **Importing a file with no bookmarks** shows *"No bookmarks were found in that file…"* rather than a silent no-op or error.

**Boundary conditions**
- **Items-per-page = All** shows everything with no "Show more"; a page size larger than your collection also shows everything.
- **Bulk-selecting then narrowing** — selection clears when the shown set changes (already approved), so counts never go stale.
- **A PDF link with extra bits** like `…/a.pdf?v=2` is still detected as a PDF for offline saving.

**Error / exception states**
- **Offline copy + archive**: archiving a bookmark **keeps** its offline copy (badge still shows in the Archived view); **deleting** it removes the bookmark and its copy together.
- **Import duplicates and undated/untagged entries** are handled as approved (skip duplicates; fill missing date with today).

**Temporal**
- **"Recently updated"** ordering reflects the most recent change; bulk changes and status changes update it too, consistent with what you approved.

Two small confirmations before I bring the whole scope back:
- **Duplicate saved-search names are allowed** (I don't block two saves with the same name). Fine, or should names be unique?
- When a **saved search's tag no longer exists**, it simply returns no results (rather than warning the saved search is "stale"). Acceptable?

If these sit right, I'll assemble the complete scope and ask for your go-ahead to build.

I’d prefer saved-search names to be unique so two identical-looking chips can’t be confused. If I reuse a name, prompt me to choose another rather than silently creating a duplicate.

A saved search referring to a tag that no longer exists can simply return no results. It isn’t broken, and it should start matching again if that tag is used later.

The rest of the edge-case behaviour sounds right. Please bring back the complete scope.

The unique-name rule is in and everything is recorded. Here's the **complete settled scope** for your bookmark app — 19 flows across saving, finding, organising, and managing. In plain terms:

**Saving & recognising**
- Save a link fast (one box, one click), with a quick editable review of the page's fetched title, description, preview image and icon.
- Duplicates send you to the existing entry to edit; a mistyped non-address is gently refused (and your text kept); a page whose details won't load can still be saved with your own title.
- Edit any field later — title, description, address, reading status, tags, notes.

**Finding**
- Live, case-insensitive search across title, description, address, tags and notes, with highlights and a full-collection count.
- Precise queries: "exact phrases", AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, and `#tag` — operators work in any case; quotes force a literal.
- Save a search (text + included/excluded tags) under a unique name and reopen it anytime.

**Organising**
- A **To read** list you can mark read; a **Reference** view (everything not to-read).
- **Archive**/restore to hide without losing; permanent **Delete** with a clear, distinct confirmation.
- Freeform **tags** with tidy normalising and autocomplete from your existing tags; **Markdown notes** that render formatted, collapse when long, and stay searchable.

**Managing at scale**
- **Sort** by date added, recently updated, or title.
- **Bulk actions** on selected bookmarks (tag/untag, mark read/unread, archive, delete) with safeguards so you never touch hidden or whole-collection items by accident.
- **Offline copy** per bookmark (page snapshot or the PDF itself) and manual **Internet Archive** submission.
- **Import/export** standard browser-bookmarks files, keeping titles, tags and dates.
- **Display preferences**: default sort, items-per-page (display-only, with Show more), and text size.

**Scope boundaries**
- A private, single-person app reachable from your computer and phone; **no sign-in** this cycle.
- Deferred (recorded, not built now): visual polish, large-collection performance tuning, and possible future importing of live browser tabs.

The prototype at **http://maker:4001** demonstrates all of this behaviourally (with simulated page-fetching, offline capture and Archive submission, since a prototype can't reach live pages).

The application is built and verified. Here's the acceptance report.

## The software is ready for your review at **http://maker:4000**

It's the real application (not the prototype): a private, single-person bookmark manager with a Node server, durable storage, and a browser front-end. It opens on the first-run empty state — paste a link to begin, or use **Import…** to bring in a browser bookmarks file.

One honest note about this review environment: it has no outbound internet, so live page-detail fetching and offline capture can't reach real external sites here. When a page can't be fetched, the app uses the approved **save-anyway fallback** (you type the title). All the automated tests exercise fetching/offline/archive against a local test site, so those behaviours are verified to work when the network is available.

## Verification outcome — all passing

I verified the implementation against every approved scenario (SCN-001–019) at three levels:

- **Acceptance tests (9, Playwright driving the real UI):** save-with-review, duplicate-opens-existing, search + boolean queries + highlighting, reading-list/archive/delete, tags + Markdown notes, bulk actions with selection-clears-on-search, saved searches with unique names, sorting + display preferences (pagination display-only), and offline copy — **all pass**.
- **Integration tests (11, real HTTP API):** metadata fetch + fallback, create/duplicate/edit/delete lifecycle, offline page-snapshot vs PDF preservation, honest capture-failure reporting, bulk scoping, import (add/skip-duplicates/keep dates & tags), no-bookmarks import message, saved-search uniqueness, preference persistence, manual Archive submission, and durability across reloads — **all pass**.
- **Unit tests (27):** URL/duplicate/PDF rules, tag normalisation, the full search query language, sort comparators, safe Markdown, and import/export round-trips — **all pass**.

**Total: 47 automated checks, 0 failures.** The implementation lives in `/work/implementation/` with the design record (`DESIGN.md`) and scenario→code map (`SCENARIO_MAP.md`) for future changes.

## What's included
Everything in the approved scope: fast save with editable review, duplicate handling, edit any field; live case-insensitive search with phrases/AND/OR/NOT/parentheses/`#tag`; reading-list, reference view, archive/restore, permanent delete with confirmation; tags with autocomplete and Markdown notes; sorting, bulk actions with whole-collection safeguards, per-bookmark offline copy and manual Internet Archive submission, import/export, and display preferences — all built from the approved specifications, not the prototype.

**Do you accept this software as implementing the behaviour we approved, on the basis of this verification report?** Once you confirm, I'll complete the cycle and record it in the session log. If anything doesn't match an approved scenario, tell me and I'll correct it within this cycle.
